newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-CORA PACES 17-HIT ATTACK AS MARINERS CRUSH ANGELS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CORA PACES 17-HIT ATTACK AS MARINERS CRUSH ANGELS.

text.p: Joey Cora went 4-for-4 with a homer and a double to pace a 17-hit attack and Jamie Moyer won his fourth straight start as the Seattle Mariners crushed the Anaheim Angels 13-4 on Monday.
Cora drove in three runs and scored three more while extending his hitting streak to 15 games as the Mariners snapped a four-game losing streak.

Cora, who belted a solo homer in the fifth inning off Anaheim starter Mark Langston to snap a 3-3 tie, is batting .475 (29-for-61) during the streak. This marked the sixth four-hit game in his career.
Jay Buhner added a two-run homer off Langston in a three-run sixth and Paul Sorrento highlighted a six-run eighth with a two-run blast off reliever Allen Watson.
Moyer (4-0) allowed four runs and seven hits in six innings as the Mariners captured their major-league best 14th road victory.

Dave Hollins smacked a three-run homer off Moyer in the first inning that briefly gave Anaheim a 3-0 lead. Seattle answered with three in the second on an RBI single by Russ Davis and a two-run double Cora.
Langston (2-3) gave up seven runs and six hits over 5 2/3 innings to take the loss. The left-hander has failed to reach the seventh inning in seven of his last eight starts.
Garret Anderson's single in the fourth inning extended his hitting streak to 14 games for the Angels, who had their seven-game winning streak stopped.
